headline: President Clinton created an emergency board to look into a labor dispute between American Airlines and its pilots' union.
what_it_does: This order set up a special emergency board to investigate a dispute between American Airlines and its pilots, who were represented by the Allied Pilots Association. Emergency boards like this are used under federal labor law for airlines and railroads. They study a dispute and report back to the President. While this process runs, the two sides generally must hold off on strikes or other major changes for a set period of time.

who_it_affects.group: American Airlines pilots represented by the Allied Pilots Association
who_it_affects.how: Their dispute with the airline was sent to a federal board for review, which generally delays a strike while the board does its work.
The company's dispute with its pilots was placed under review by a federal board, which generally limits changes it can make during that time.
Creating the board was aimed at keeping the airline's flights running while the dispute was reviewed.
